record_notes:
Account summary
- KiteLedger is evaluating Redwood Dedicated for an EU-resident, multi-tenant customer support assistant + internal ops summarization.
- They tested Hosted briefly, but target is EU-only Dedicated with VPC peering (they’re sensitive to noisy-neighbor + want predictable throughput).
- Recent escalation: TP workloads intermittently hang under sustained streaming + high concurrency (eu-west). They want an explicit stability plan + hotfix timeline before moving to procurement.

Firmographics / buying context
- EU HQ (Germany + UK teams). Security team is centralized; procurement requires SOC2 package + DPA + EU data residency confirmation.
- Budget is approved “in principle” for inference spend if p95 latency and uptime commitments are clear.

Workload + technical requirements (from calls + tickets)
- Primary workload: chat + tool-calling style prompts, streaming responses.
- Secondary: summarization of long tickets and KYC ops notes (bursty).
- Model shape: large open-weight model w/ TP (they referenced TP=8 as target, with room to scale to TP=16 later).
- Context: 16k baseline; roadmap includes 32k for a subset of flows.
- Concurrency target: ~150-250 concurrent streams during peaks; mixed sequence lengths (many short, some long-running).
- Latency: p95 time-to-first-token < 800ms on interactive flows; steady-state token rate consistent (they track “token cadence” drop-offs as user-visible issue).
- Reliability: they are strict on “no hangs”; timeouts must fail fast and retry/fallback cleanly. Quote from escalation call: “A single stuck group can take out an entire shard and we can’t explain that to ops.”
- Routing/fallback: wants policy-based fallback to a smaller compatible variant (same API surface) when a pool is degraded.

Current status / stage
- Stage: Evaluation (close to Procurement if stability is proven on their canary).
- They will not sign until we demonstrate the TP hang mitigations in eu-west, and we provide operational runbook + alerting hooks.

Recent activity timeline (high signal)
- 2025-02-13/14: Impact review after TP hang incident pattern discussed internally (shared that we’re treating as top runtime priority). Linked: Gmail thread thread-2025-02-14_tp-hang-sev1-followups.
- 2025-02-18: Customer asked if they can get a hotfix build for eu-west; we aligned internally on go/no-go criteria for runtime 1.19 hotfix. Linked: thread-2025-02-18_runtime-1-19-hotfix-go-no-go_tp-stability.
- 2025-02-20: Technical deep dive with their platform + ML infra leads. Fireflies: ff-2025-02-20_technical-deep-dive_tp-stability.
  - We walked through suspected failure modes (collective stalls vs scheduler/barrier deadlocks under cancellation) and mitigation plan (watchdog + quarantine + async error propagation).
  - They requested: explicit default settings by deployment mode (Hosted vs Dedicated), and how we avoid false positives that reset healthy groups.
- 2025-02-23 to 2025-02-26: Support triage + log exchanges. Tickets referenced: SUP-9827, SUP-9841.
- 2025-02-27: Escalation call with CS + SRE + Runtime. Fireflies: ff-2025-02-27_customer-escalation_tp-timeouts.
  - Agreed on a controlled canary: limited traffic slice in eu-west, enable watchdog/quarantine metrics + dashboards; daily check-in until stable.

Escalation details (condensed)
- Symptoms reported
  - Streaming requests stall (no tokens) while TCP connections remain open; client eventually times out.
  - Cluster appears “up” but throughput collapses; a subset of TP groups never recover without restart.
  - In some events, retries amplify load and worsen the stall.
- Environment notes (from SUP tickets)
  - Deployment: Dedicated (eu-west). TP enabled.
  - Workload pattern: sustained high concurrency, mixed prompt lengths, many client disconnects (browser/app timeouts).
  - They shared NCCL-like stall signatures and scheduler “no forward progress” messages (see log sample refs in Drive link).
- Impact
  - Customer-visible timeouts on their beta; internal SRE escalated due to oncall pages.
  - They paused expanding traffic to Redwood until fix is in place.

What we promised / positioning used
- We are implementing TP-group health model and a forward-progress watchdog that quarantines stuck groups so they stop receiving work.
- Hardened async error propagation for collectives so we fail fast instead of silently stalling.
- Cancellation-safe barrier semantics so client disconnects don’t deadlock a TP group.
- Improved observability: per-rank progress, collective latency histograms, and structured logs for “comm stall vs kernel stall vs scheduler starvation.”

Key stakeholders (customer side)
- VP Platform Engineering (owner of inference runtime decision).
- ML Infra lead (cares about throughput/cost; very skeptical of “just restart the node” mitigations).
- Security lead (focused on EU data residency and audit log retention).

- Clarify audit log retention expectations (they mentioned 12 months, may require add-on).

1) Redwood to provide recommended Dedicated defaults for:
